note: Pipeline C step 1 for the ten held-no-photo spots of the Wellington region. Bios are drafts for use if photos are found. Facts are limited to what the cited pages said when loaded. Prices and hours are from the operator where one was loaded; otherwise unverified.

entries.name: The Wool Shed National Museum of Sheep and Shearing
entries.recommendation: keep (strong of the ten): a real, staffed, ticketed museum with an operator site; the only thing holding it back is a photo
entries.overlap: Separate from Aratoi (wairarapa-12); sits next to it and Queen Elizabeth Park in Masterton. Placement: Wairarapa spot.
entries.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Masterton listing (-40.94897, 175.6647) and OSM way 1153427491 (tourism=museum, 12 Dixon Street) agree to 10 m
entries.bio_draft: A volunteer-run, hands-on museum in Masterton on the history, culture and sport of sheep shearing, with a Golden Shears Wall of Fame and a wool shop.

bio_facts.fact: Hands-on heritage museum run by a voluntary trust in Masterton; also a community venue
Presents the industry, culture and sport of shearing in NZ; 160 years of shearing history; virtual shearers, wool handling and shearing equipment
Free entry to the Golden Shears Wall of Fame and the retail shop
Shearing and spinning demonstrations only by prior arrangement for groups of 10 or more

entries.hours: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Mon–Fri; 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM weekends and public holidays; closed Christmas Day, Good Friday and ANZAC Day
entries.hours_source: https://www.thewoolshednz.com/visit-us (the Destination Wairarapa page says 10am-4pm 7 days; the operator page is used)
entries.closedDays_suggestion: none weekly; specialClosures would be Dec 25 only (Good Friday and ANZAC Day move or vary)

cost.note: adult; child under 15 $5; family $25; under 5 free. Wikivoyage's $8 is older (2017) and superseded

entries.ticketUrl_check: Loaded; page title 'NZ sheep and shearing museum, with a wool products shop.' Heading 'Welcome to New Zealand's museum of sheep and shearing'. Also linked as the operator from wairarapanz.com listing. thewoolshednz.com redirects to www.
entries.discrepancies: Home page footer says 10 Dixon Street; Visit Us page, OSM and Wikivoyage say 12 Dixon Street (opposite Queen Elizabeth Park, next to the iSite).

entries.name: Honeycomb Rock
entries.recommendation: keep as a standalone spot (DOC page + Destination Wairarapa); caveats: remote, 5-6 h return walk on private farmland, closed for lambing Sep-Oct. Only a fit, determined visitor goes, so rank low. Weakest on the 'visitor can actually do something' test but passes (coastal walk, seal colony, shipwreck).
entries.overlap: None. Not within Wairarapa destination's likely span (about 60 km from Masterton on the east coast).
entries.coordinates_source: OSM node 619736995 (natural=cliff, tourism=viewpoint, name=Honeycomb Rock; Nominatim lookup -41.3601176, 175.8104765). This is the rock itself, reached on foot; the walkway starts inside Glenburn Station to the north (OSM way 46046365 'Honeycomb Rock Walking Track' runs from -41.3196, 175.8488 to -41.3490, 175.8191). A visitor-standing-point trailhead coordinate could not be confirmed from a source; unverified.
entries.bio_draft: A coastal outcrop weathered into a cell-like honeycomb pattern, reached on a flat 5-6 hour return coastal walk across Glenburn Station, passing a fur seal colony and the wreck of the Tuvalu.

bio_facts.fact: Coastal rock outcrop weathered into a honeycomb pattern; reached by walking the coastline
Walkway is flat and easy, along the coast across farmland, about 5-6 hours return; entirely within privately owned Glenburn Station (keep to marked track, do not disturb stock)
Wreck of the Fijian trader Tuvalu, aground on its maiden voyage on 11 January 1967, lies a few metres south of the rock
Fur seal colony about halfway along the walk, peaking in winter
No toilets, bins or drinking water; no dogs; track closed for lambing in September and October (one third-party guide says Aug-Sep)
About 60 km from Masterton via Whiti Rd, Te Wharau Rd and Glenburn Rd to Glenburn Station

entries.hours: Daylight, Open 24 hours not appropriate; suggest 'Daylight hours; walkway closed for lambing Sep–Oct'
entries.visit_hours_basis: walk time from Destination Wairarapa page

cost.note: no fee found on DOC or Destination Wairarapa pages; access across private land, confirm with Glenburn Station. unverified

entries.ticketUrl_check: Loaded; title 'Honeycomb Rock area: Places to go in the Wairarapa', body describes Honeycomb Rock. DOC is the agency listing the walkway though the land is private.
entries.standalone_fields_needed: country New Zealand, NZ, Oceania, Pacific/Auckland; id slug e.g. honeycomb-rock

entries.name: Colonial Knob (Rangituhi)
entries.recommendation: keep: three counted sources (Wikivoyage, DOC, WellingtonNZ); a steep half-day walk with 360-degree views and part of Te Araroa
entries.overlap: None with existing spots in Porirua; Belmont Regional Park is a separate park. Placement: Wellington spot (Porirua is within the Wellington span only if defaultZoomSpanKm allows; check ~15 km from city centre, about 12 km north-west... verify with span rule).
entries.coordinates_source: Camp Elsdon, 18 Raiha Street, Elsdon (OSM camp_site via Nominatim); WellingtonNZ says most walkers start at the Camp Elsdon car park, DOC says access is via Broken Hill Road off Raiha Street. Summit (Wikipedia) 41°09'13"S 174°48'14"E = -41.1536, 174.8039; Wikivoyage lookout listing -41.143662, 174.811438. Use the trailhead for the pin.
entries.bio_draft: A 468 m hill above Porirua, climbed by a steep track from Elsdon to a lookout with views of Mana and Kāpiti islands, Porirua Harbour and, on a clear day, Mount Taranaki.

bio_facts.fact: Summit 468 m; views to the Inland Kaikōura Range to the south, Mt Taranaki to the north-west, Mana and Kāpiti islands and Porirua Harbour
Early Māori name Rangituhi means 'sky glow', from the red glow of the hill at sunset; walkway is part of Te Araroa
Track to the lookout is 1.6 km return with 310 m of ascent (steep); most people start at Camp Elsdon car park; dogs not permitted
Wikivoyage: may get snow in winter, a few hours' walk for great views of Cook Strait

entries.discrepancies: WellingtonNZ lists 1.6 km return to the lookout (highest point 347 m); the 468 m summit is farther on. Use 'a few hours' only if going to the summit. Check time before quoting.
entries.hours_source: public reserve; no hours published on DOC or WellingtonNZ pages (unverified)
entries.visit_hours_basis: estimate: lookout vs summit; Wikivoyage 'a few hours'
entries.ticketUrl_check: Loaded; title 'Rangituhi/Colonial Knob Scenic Reserve: Places to go in Wellington and Kapiti', content about the reserve

entries.name: Skyline Walkway
entries.recommendation: keep (two counted sources; Wellington City Council operates it; it crosses Mount Kaukau and links to Te Araroa). Possible overlap if Mount Kaukau or Makara Peak ever become spots; it is a long linear feature, so pin at one named access point.
entries.overlap: None with current spots (no Kaukau or Makara Peak spot found in spots.ts search for these names).
entries.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Wellington/City listing (-41.2723, 174.7048), the Mākara Saddle end. Alternatives: Mount Kaukau summit -41.2315, 174.7779 (OSM peak; on the route, access off Woodmancote Rd, Khandallah); OSM track node near Karori -41.2727, 174.7353. Choose one by span rule; the Kaukau end is the easier visitor access (train to Khandallah per Wikivoyage). Not verified against a trailhead car park.
entries.bio_draft: A ridge-top walkway along Wellington's outer green belt from Johnsonville past Mount Kaukau to Mākara Saddle, with views over the whole region and a link to Te Araroa.

bio_facts.fact: Runs along the ridge tops from Johnsonville south-west to Mākara Saddle, Karori; WCC (via OSM): about 12 km, up to 5 hours, following the Outer Green Belt; operator Wellington City Council

WellingtonNZ lists 18.2 km, about 7 hours, 900 m climb, highest point 432 m, if extended to Churton Park/Mākara Peak; part of Te Araroa; dogs on lead; no toilets or water; follow purple markers; also used by mountain bikers (Grade 4)
Wikivoyage: 12 km, 5-6 hr challenging walk
Mount Kaukau (455 m, 122 m TV mast) is a lookout on the route, reached from Woodmancote Road, Khandallah

entries.discrepancies: Length is 12 km (WCC/OSM/Wikivoyage) vs 18.2 km (WellingtonNZ, which includes extensions). Use 'about 12 km' in the bio if citing WCC.
entries.visit_hours_basis: 5-6 h (Wikivoyage), 7 h (WellingtonNZ); can also be walked in sections
entries.ticketUrl_check: UNVERIFIED: this is the operator page named in OSM relation 9286961 and Wikivoyage, but it returns 403 to scripts (curl and WebFetch), so its title could not be checked. Fallback verified page: https://wellingtonnz.com/visit/trails/skyline-walkway (title 'Skyline Walkway in Wellington – WellingtonNZ', a tourism board page, not the operator). Per WRITING.md: leave ticketUrl out unless checked in a real browser.

entries.name: Hemi Matenga Scenic Reserve
entries.recommendation: keep: three counted sources; 30 ha kohekohe forest walks above Waikanae with a Kāpiti Island view; closer to a real destination for walkers than the Waikanae town entry
entries.overlap: Sits in Waikanae; Ngā Manu and Waikanae Beach are separate. Te Au Track summit 521 m is the same height as the Kāpiti Island summit figure in kapiti-coast-1 (coincidence; WellingtonNZ gives 521 m, Wellington Regional Trails gives 523 m).
entries.coordinates_source: Tūī Crescent, Waikanae, the reserve's main entrance per DOC and WellingtonNZ (Nominatim street point -40.8746647, 175.0763019). Reserve centroid OSM 'Hemi Matenga Memorial Park Scenic Reserve' -40.8696672, 175.0869004 (protected area, not the entrance). Street centroid, not the exact gate; accurate to about 100-200 m (unverified).
entries.bio_draft: A 30-hectare scenic reserve above Waikanae with an easy loop through one of New Zealand's largest remaining stands of kohekohe forest and steeper tracks with views of Kāpiti Island and the estuary.

bio_facts.fact: 30 ha of native forest, one of the largest remaining areas of kohekohe forest in NZ; views of Kāpiti Island and the Waikanae Estuary
Kohekohe Walk easy 30-min loop (about 1 km); Parata Track 1-2 h return (1.8 km); Te Au Track 2-4 h return (2.8 km), climbing to 521 m; full circuit 2-3 h from the Huia St entrance
Main entrance Tūī Crescent with small car park by a reservoir; second entrance Kakariki Grove; dogs on a leash; Waikanae station about 15 min walk to Parata Track
Wikivoyage: steep walk with a view of Kāpiti Island, good mountain biking and walking tracks

entries.discrepancies: Official name varies: 'Hemi Matenga Memorial Park Scenic Reserve' (DOC), 'Hemi Matenga Scenic Reserve' (WellingtonNZ), 'Hemi Matanga' (a WellingtonNZ town page typo). Te Au highest point 521 m vs 523 m.
entries.ticketUrl_check: Loaded; title 'Kohekohe Walk: Waikanae area, Kapiti region.' and body names Hemi Matenga Memorial Park Scenic Reserve. It is a DOC page for a walk in the reserve, but DOC does not state it manages the reserve; the reserve-level page https://www.wellingtonnz.com/visit/trails/hemi-matenga-scenic-reserve (title 'Hemi Matenga Scenic Reserve, Kāpiti Coast – WellingtonNZ') is the tourism board, not a steward. Weak: treat as acceptable only if the owner accepts a DOC walk page; otherwise omit.

entries.name: Petone
entries.recommendation: review / marginal keep. A seaside suburb, not an attraction. The distinct draws are the Esplanade and swimmable foreshore plus the Jackson Street strip, but the strongest sight (Petone Settlers Museum) is already wellington-28. If kept, restrict the bio to the foreshore and Jackson Street and rank it low; otherwise drop. Wikipedia: Britannia 1840 history.
entries.overlap: Overlaps Petone Settlers Museum (wellington-28, -41.22927, 174.88018). Also existing bio for wellington-28 says 'on Petone Wharf': WellingtonNZ says the museum is 'halfway along the Esplanade' and Wikipedia says Petone Wharf was closed Jan 2021 after earthquake damage (still closed Aug 2025). Suggest correcting wellington-28's bio to 'on the Petone Esplanade'.
entries.coordinates_source: The Esplanade, Petone (Nominatim -41.2283137, 174.8773253), the foreshore road. Wikipedia suburb point -41.225, 174.878. Jackson Street (secondary road) -41.2253563, 174.8787336. All approximate.
entries.bio_draft: A seaside suburb on Wellington Harbour where the first European settlers landed in 1840, with a shallow sandy beach, the Esplanade and an 800 m Jackson Street strip of cafés, bars and vintage shops.

bio_facts.fact: Wellington's first colonial settlement (1840); formerly a fortified Māori pā; beachside walking trails; Esplanade views across harbour and Cook Strait and start of the Hutt River Trail
Jackson Street: more than 60 bars, cafés and restaurants in 800 m, plus vintage clothing, book, record and furniture stores
Te Puna Wai Ora sculpture on Buick Street gives free artesian water
Shallow sandy foreshore formed by Hutt River sediment, popular family swimming spot; Jackson Street is a Heritage NZ historic area; Petone Wharf (1908-09) closed since January 2021
Wikivoyage: first colonial settlement; Petone beach popular for swimming and water sports

entries.discrepancies: Wikipedia notes a 2024 council vote to rename the suburb Pito One, declined by the Minister in December 2024; the name stays Petone.
entries.hours_source: open-access beach and street; shops vary
entries.ticketUrl_check: None: a suburb with no one steward.

entries.name: Ōtaki
entries.recommendation: review. The town is named by two counted sources, but its sights are Rangiātea Church (a 2003 replica of the 1851 church burned in 1995; public access and hours not found), the free Ōtaki Museum (site not reachable) and Ōtaki Beach (already kapiti-coast-8). If kept, make it 'Rangiātea Church' or 'Ōtaki' with a bio of the church and Māori identity; otherwise drop. Needs a second source for open-to-visitors on Rangiātea before a spot.
entries.overlap: Overlaps Ōtaki Beach (kapiti-coast-8) only through the name; Ōtaki Forks/Tararua Southern Crossing standalone is separate.
entries.coordinates_source: Rangiātea Church, Te Rauparaha Street (OSM place_of_worship -40.7500191, 175.1375653; Wikivoyage -40.750028, 175.137642; Wikipedia 40°45'0.1"S 175°8'15.5"E). Town centre alternative -40.7526, 175.1391 (Ōtaki Museum, 49 Main St, Wikivoyage) or -40.753, 175.14 (Wikipedia).
entries.bio_draft: The northernmost Kāpiti Coast town, one of Aotearoa's most bilingual, home to Rangiātea Church (rebuilt in 2003 after a 1995 arson), Te Wānanga o Raukawa and a free local museum.

bio_facts.fact: Northernmost Kāpiti Coast town; 'one of Aotearoa's most bilingual towns'; named attractions: Rangiātea Church, Ōtaki Forks, Te Wānanga o Raukawa, Māoriland Hub, Ōtaki Beach, Hori Gallery
Rangiātea: built 1844-51 under Te Rauparaha and Octavius Hadfield; arson 7 October 1995, oldest Māori Anglican church in NZ at the time; replica completed 2003
Ōtaki Museum, 49 Main St, free (Wikivoyage 2017 listing; hours not listed; url http://www.otakimuseum.co.nz/ did not load)
Ōtaki-Māori Racing Club, 47 Te Roto Rd, described as the only Māori horse-racing club in NZ (an event venue, not a spot)

entries.hours: Check operator for hours (church and museum hours not found)
entries.ticketUrl_check: None verified. Ōtaki Museum URL from Wikivoyage (otakimuseum.co.nz, http and https, with and without www) did not respond (curl status 000). A town has no single official site. UNVERIFIED if the owner chooses to spot the museum or church.

entries.name: Waikanae
entries.recommendation: drop the town as a spot (or fold in). The two real draws are already spots (Waikanae Beach kapiti-coast-11, Ngā Manu kapiti-coast-9) and Hemi Matenga (above) is the best remaining one. A town centre of shops and a 1907 post-office museum open Fri-Sun 1-4 PM is not a half-hour reason to stop. If the owner wants it, a better spot is Waikanae Estuary Scientific Reserve (DOC, 60+ bird species) not a town pin.
entries.overlap: Overlaps Waikanae Beach (kapiti-coast-11), Ngā Manu (kapiti-coast-9) and Hemi Matenga; all attractions in the town are separate spots.
entries.coordinates_source: Wikipedia suburb point; Wikivoyage station -40.876667, 175.066111; Kāpiti Coast Museum -40.87794, 175.06706. Town centre only.
entries.bio_draft: A relaxed beach town of about 14,000 on the Waikanae River, gateway to Hemi Matenga's bush walks, the estuary's bird reserve and the river trail.

bio_facts.fact: Laid-back beach town of about 14,000 (2022) with a gardening community; trains from Wellington about 1 hour
Waikanae River Trail: flat gravel path on both sides of the river with safe swimming spots; river and estuary home to many native birds; Hemi Matenga Scenic Reserve bush walks
Kāpiti Coast Museum, 9 Elizabeth St, Fri-Sun 1-4 PM, by donation, in the 1907 post office (2022-era listing)

entries.ticketUrl_check: None: a town with no single steward.

entries.name: Paraparaumu
entries.recommendation: drop as a separate spot. The name is a town of shops (Coastlands) and services; Wikivoyage itself does not say the town centre is a draw; every attraction people go for is already a spot: Paraparaumu Beach (kapiti-coast-6), Southward Car Museum (kapiti-coast-5), Kāpiti Island (kapiti-coast-1), Queen Elizabeth Park (kapiti-coast-9) and Raumati Beach (kapiti-coast-4). Fails 'venue that is only a shop' and near-duplicate tests.
entries.overlap: Heavy overlap with Paraparaumu Beach (-40.89148, 174.98129 in kapiti-coast-6), whose bio already covers the Kāpiti Island departure point, and with Southward Car Museum.
entries.coordinates_source: Wikipedia and Wikivoyage town point. A town centre; Coastlands mall not geocoded.
entries.bio_draft: The Kāpiti Coast's largest town and unofficial capital, the base for the beach, Southward Car Museum and Kāpiti Island boats.

bio_facts.fact: Largest township on the Kāpiti Coast with the most shops and services, called the 'unofficial capital of the Kāpiti Coast'; Coastlands has 50+ stores and a cinema
Southward Car Museum about 5 min from the centre; Paraparaumu Beach is the departure point for Kāpiti Island boats
Wikivoyage calls it a good stop to refuel; Statue of Our Lady of Lourdes (14 m, behind the railway station) is called uninspiring
Saturday morning market at Paraparaumu Beach (weekly, excluded by COVERAGE.md)

entries.ticketUrl_check: None: a town with no single steward.

entries.name: Masterton
entries.recommendation: drop as a separate spot / low-value. Masterton is the Wairarapa hub, but the destination is already Wairarapa, which already lists Aratoi (wairarapa-12) and Mount Holdsworth, and the new Wool Shed entry gives the town its one distinct draw. The town (Wikipedia: about 22,600 people) has no half-hour sight of its own beyond those and Queen Elizabeth Park (20+ ha, 1875 giant sequoia, miniature railway, cricket ground; Wikivoyage's link for it is dead). If kept it must be a low-rank base entry only; the owner can decide.
entries.overlap: Contains Aratoi (wairarapa-12), the Wool Shed (above) and Queen Elizabeth Park; the closest spot is Aratoi, 600 m from the Wool Shed.
entries.coordinates_source: Wikipedia and Wikivoyage town point. Queen Elizabeth Park (Wikivoyage) -40.9495, 175.6686, opposite the Wool Shed.
entries.bio_draft: The Wairarapa's largest town, with an art and history museum, the national sheep and shearing museum and a historic park, and the base for Mount Holdsworth and the Tararua tracks.

bio_facts.fact: Largest town in the Wairarapa, about 100 km north-east of Wellington; about 22,600 people in the urban area (June 2025)
Hosts the annual Golden Shears sheep-shearing competition
Queen Elizabeth Park: 20+ hectares with giant sequoias planted in 1875, cricket ground and a miniature railway opened in 1972
Aratoi: Bruce St, daily 10 AM–4 PM, gold coin donation (Wikivoyage 2018)

entries.ticketUrl_check: None: a town with no single steward. (Masterton District Council has a site, not an attraction site; not linked.)

marginal_review: Petone (beach and Jackson Street; also correct wellington-28's 'on Petone Wharf')
